title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry
scope: Verified research routes for the history of physical microscope slides and preparations. The registry includes archives, manuscript fonds, society archives, slide collections with documentary apparatus, trade and institutional archives, and major digital primary-source portals. Inclusion is a route to evidence, not an assertion that every holding contains nineteenth-century slides or that a surviving object is identical with a historical record.

relations.direct: The described holding explicitly contains microscope slides/preparations, a slide catalogue/index, or correspondence/documentation tied to a slide-producing or slide-circulating actor.
relations.contextual: The holding is highly relevant to microscopy, instruments, scientific production, institutional custody, or preparation practice, but a slide-specific archival bridge still has to be demonstrated.
relations.portal: A digital primary-source portal useful for locating historical printed or administrative evidence rather than a single archival fonds.

records.holdings: The Club states that its archives and slide collection are stored at the Natural History Museum; a current transcription project describes more than 20,000 microscope slides.
records.research_use: Club subscriptions, donations, exhibitions, labels, maker attributions, cabinet order, and the institutional afterlife of publications such as Arthur C. Cole's Studies in Microscopical Science.
records.access: Archive/collection access by enquiry; journal issues 1868–2012 are separately available digitally.

records.holdings: The Museum describes about 150,000 microscope slides within a diatom collection of more than 300,000 specimens, together with handwritten notes, letters, sketches and drawings, index-card files, micrographs, and exsiccata sets.
records.research_use: High-value object↔text route for Greville, Kützing, William Smith, Kitton, Ralfs, Deby and other nineteenth-century diatomists; supports label, locality, series, and provenance crosswalks.
records.access: Research access through the collection curator; specimen records are progressively available through the NHM Data Portal.

records.date_scope: historical collections; cataloguing files include twentieth-century layers
records.holdings: The archives include correspondence and papers of the Diatom Section. One open file is explicitly catalogued as 'Catalogue and lists of microscope slides' and includes an Index to Diatom Slides and lists of types and museum slides.
records.research_use: Reconstructs how historical slide collections were indexed, renamed, and transferred into museum catalogue systems; useful companion to the physical diatom collection.
records.access: Open archive material subject to NHM Archives access procedures.

records.institution: University of Sheffield Special Collections and Archives
records.holdings: Documents relating to Henry Clifton Sorby include diaries, a letter, architectural photographs, and reprinted papers with manuscript amendments.
records.research_use: Primary route into Sorby's working chronology and revisions. Especially relevant to microscopic petrology, metallography, material preparation, and the movement between specimen, section, observation, and publication.
records.access: Reading-room access by appointment; photographs are digitised online.

records.institution: University of St Andrews Libraries and Museums
records.collection: Papers of D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson — Rousselet/Hood correspondence
records.holdings: A described group of letters and additional documents concerns C. F. Rousselet's methods, J. Hood, D'Arcy Thompson, and the Quekett Microscopical Club; the file includes a sketch and a typed list relating to Rousselet's Rotifera work.
records.research_use: A late-nineteenth-century route into preparation methods, rotifer work, correspondence networks, and the movement of microscopical technique through clubs and university zoology.
records.access: Special Collections archival record; consultation subject to St Andrews access conditions.

records.holdings: The archive preserves administrative and scientific records from the Station's foundation, including correspondence, general-affairs registers, copybooks, manuscripts, offprints, photographs, films, drawings, and other institutional records.
records.research_use: Highest-priority archive for the Naples preparation department, laboratory users, commercial preparation traffic, specimen supply, correspondence, and the object routes already identified in the 1880 catalogue/RMS case.
records.access: Open by appointment for scholarly research; consultation and reproduction services are available.

records.collection: Carl Zeiss Jena archives and historical production/supply lists
records.holdings: Original records, files, photographs, patents, product literature, technical documentation, and instruments. Digitised microscope production and dispatch books record serial/stand number, recipient, place of delivery, accessories, delivery date, and production information.
records.research_use: Allows microscope users and institutions in the slide corpus to be linked to instrument acquisition and distribution. Useful for testing whether slide exchange and instrument supply travelled through the same institutional networks.
records.access: Archive research by arrangement; historic microscope production/supply lists are searchable online.

records.collection: Archives and scientific collections of the Musée Dupuytren
records.holdings: The university preserves the historical pathological-anatomy collections of the Musée Dupuytren together with associated medical archives and scientific heritage.
records.research_use: Potential route into pathology teaching, specimen preparation, histological practice, and the relation between microscopic preparations and larger anatomical museum systems.
records.access: Scientific heritage collections are accessible on motivated research request; the historical museum closed in 2016 and its collections remain under university custody.

records.holdings: More than 300 archival collections covering early Pasteur collaborators through later scientists; records include manuscripts, correspondence, laboratory notebooks, teaching material, mission and experimental papers, photographs, and institutional records.
records.research_use: Strong route for medical microscopy, bacteriology, laboratory preparation, equipment purchases, and the movement of microscopic methods into institutional biomedical science. The Pasteur Museum separately preserves historic instruments including Pasteur's Nachet microscope.
records.access: Reading-room consultation by appointment; pre-1940 management/department records are generally open, with later/private holdings subject to conditions.

records.holdings: The Repertorium documents the historical Zoological Museum collection and its institutional/library traces. Ambrosius A. W. Hubrecht is recorded as a director associated with major improvements to the museum from the late 1880s.
records.research_use: Institutional route for the Hubrecht material already present in the surviving-object survey; useful for separating museum, laboratory, library, and later custodial layers.
records.access: Repertorium and Utrecht University Special Collections provide catalogue and consultation routes.

records.collection: Hubrecht preservation instructions and Netherlands Indies embryological programme
records.holdings: Utrecht University Repository records Hubrecht's 1891 instructions for preserving embryological material and related instructions for collecting material in the Netherlands Indies, with physical copies in the University Library.
records.research_use: Primary evidence for how preparative protocols were delegated across long-distance collection networks before material reached Utrecht for embryological study.
records.access: Repository metadata online; access to some full text depends on University Library conditions.

records.collection: Catalogue of microscopical slides of the Bailey collection (far00061)
records.holdings: An inventory of Jacob Whitman Bailey's microscopical slides, begun by Bailey and completed by Miss Washburn in June 1876; the volume was bequeathed to the Boston Society of Natural History and transferred to the Farlow Herbarium in 1941.
records.research_use: Exceptional historical object↔catalogue bridge: slide inventory, collector authorship, later continuation, society custody, and twentieth-century institutional transfer can be traced in one documentary object.
records.access: The fragile volume has been digitised; the finding aid provides digital content and appointment information.

records.holdings: Series I–IV, numbers 1–100, as strewn mounts on microscope slides. A handwritten catalogue titled 'F. Kitton, Hon. F.R.M.S. Norfolk Diatomaceae' is held in the Farlow Library; the slides are in General Collection 2201–2300.
records.research_use: A ready-made publication/object crosswalk linking a numbered commercial/published series to a surviving institutional set and manuscript catalogue.
records.access: Online item-level index; manuscript/library and physical-slide consultation by Farlow arrangement.

records.holdings: The Farlow holds both editions of Century I and a partial Century II set. Its index derives from slide labels and the schedule of taxa printed inside a century-box cover; second-century slides retain distinctive Eulenstein metal-ring labels.
records.research_use: Strong object-level route into edition, numbering, label design, locality change, packaging, and distributed-copy comparison across institutions.
records.access: Online catalogue and collection notes; physical access by Farlow arrangement.

records.collection: Hamilton Lanphere Smith, Diatomacearum Species Typicae
records.holdings: Centuries I–VI plus supplements, numbers 1–750. The series consists of microscope-slide strewn mounts accompanied by labelled cards identifying species and localities, normally one card for each 25 slides.
records.research_use: Direct evidence for a serial slide-publication system organized through numbered preparations and paper finding aids; useful comparator to Cole and Eulenstein.
records.access: Online series catalogue; physical materials by Farlow arrangement.

records.collection: William Almeron Terry correspondence (far00014) and Terry Collection documentation
records.holdings: A bound volume of letters sent to Terry, with photographs and printed material. Farlow documentation notes Terry's slide-making and exchange activity and links the physical Terry collection to correspondence, card catalogues, and Tempère & Peragallo references.
records.research_use: High-value exchange-network archive: correspondence can be cross-read against surviving slides, vials, localities, and published distributed series.
records.access: Finding aid online; collection available by research appointment.

records.institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History — Archives Center
records.holdings: Six cubic feet of materials assembled for the history and development of microscopes, including publications, trade literature, photographs and negatives, correspondence, conference material, bibliographies, advertising clippings, and a card catalogue.
records.research_use: Useful secondary archive for nineteenth-century manufacturers, trade literature, advertisements, and later histories of microscopes and slides; can route to primary commercial sources not preserved elsewhere.
records.access: Archives Center research by appointment; collection-level and item-level descriptions online.

records.holdings: McGill's archival catalogue has a dedicated 'Slides (microscopy)' genre and preserves scientific-object/record combinations in fonds. The University Archives also preserves historic teaching materials, including boxed microscope slides.
records.research_use: A route for integrating university teaching, pathology, geology, scientific equipment, and the archival treatment of microscope-slide objects as records rather than specimens alone.
records.access: Archival catalogue online; reading-room and repository access by McGill University Archives arrangement.

records.holdings: The division preserves permanent microscopic preparations and associated materials. The Joaquín Frenguelli diatom collection contains 2,435 microscope preparations; other important holdings include Möller and Tempère & Peragallo collections dating from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
records.research_use: Critical comparator for distributed diatom publication series, especially Tempère & Peragallo; offers a South American endpoint with associated material rather than an isolated specimen hit.
records.access: Museum division/collection access by institutional enquiry.

records.holdings: The division reports a collection of about 1,500 microscopic preparations, including cuticles, stem and wood sections, palynological preparations, and electron-microscopy stubs; 280 are type specimens.
records.research_use: Comparative material for how botanical and geological preparations were preserved, registered, and assigned type status in museum collection systems.
records.access: Museum division access by institutional enquiry.

records.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales Bernardino Rivadavia (MACN-CONICET)
records.holdings: MACN describes extensive collections produced by nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century naturalists and maintains national collections that include diatoms, foraminifera, palynology, entomology, parasitology, and microscopic preparations.
records.research_use: A broad South American route for nineteenth-century naturalist provenance, exchange and institutional succession; individual slide subcollections require separate closure before object-level claims are made.
records.access: Collection consultation and loans through relevant MACN divisions.

records.holdings: Iziko reports 5,644 microscope slides within its entomology holdings, alongside large mounted, bottled and type collections.
records.research_use: A verified African institutional endpoint for slide-mounted zoological material. Nineteenth-century provenance must be established at subcollection/object level rather than inferred from the aggregate count.
records.access: Research and collection access through Iziko Museums.

records.date_scope: institution founded 1916; predecessor Zoological Section of Indian Museum founded 1875
records.holdings: The Protozoology Section reports a large specimen repository including type slides and more than a thousand ciliate slides; the institutional lineage of ZSI begins in the Zoological Section of the Indian Museum in 1875.
records.research_use: Current repository route for Indian microscopic zoology and institutional succession. Nineteenth-century slide identity should be treated as open until catalogue or accession evidence links specific objects to the Indian Museum period.
records.access: Collection enquiries through Zoological Survey of India headquarters.

records.date_scope: Indian Museum/ZSI publications and later series
records.holdings: ZSI maintains a text-searchable digital archive of its published documents and describes its origin in the Zoological Section of the Indian Museum, established in 1875.
records.research_use: Primary routing layer for published catalogues, taxonomic records, institutional reports, and later references back to Indian Museum material; useful for reverse-searching named preparations and collections.
records.access: Search and PDF/DjVu access online.

records.institution: The University Museum, The University of Tokyo (UMUT)
records.date_scope: collections accumulated since the University's foundation in 1877
records.holdings: UMUT manages research collections across earth sciences, biological sciences and cultural history. The museum states that more than four million specimens have accumulated from university research and teaching since 1877, with searchable specialist databases for several departments.
records.research_use: Institutional route for Meiji-period teaching/research collections and later museum transfer. Slide-specific nineteenth-century material needs department-level verification before promotion to a direct relation.
records.access: Collection databases online; research access depends on department and museum procedures.

records.holdings: Digitised books, periodicals, newspapers and government publications, including public-domain Meiji materials with stable identifiers and, for many records, IIIF manifests.
records.research_use: Primary portal for Japanese-language trade advertisements, government material, catalogues, manuals and periodicals that can be searched against makers, distributors, institutions and prepared-slide terminology.
records.access: Online; access level varies by item from public Internet access to library-only or registered-user access.

records.collection: Museums Victoria Archives and natural-science collections
records.holdings: Museums Victoria describes an institutional archive preserving the Museum's organisational memory alongside long-running natural-science collections and collection databases.
records.research_use: Route into acquisition, exchange, departmental custody, labels, movements and collection-management records behind Australian microscope-slide holdings.
records.access: Collection records online; archive and research access by museum enquiry.

records.collection: William Mountier Bale Collection — hydrozoan microslides
records.holdings: Museums Victoria publishes object-level records and high-resolution images of Bale Collection hydrozoans mounted on glass microscope slides; an 1884 syntype record identifies the specimen nature explicitly as microslide.
records.research_use: Object-level Australian endpoint for nineteenth-century zoological preparation with registration numbers, taxon, collector, locality, type status and downloadable images.
records.access: Object records and large images online; physical collection currently in storage and available through museum research procedures.

records.institution: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
records.collection: Natural History collections and Te Papa Archives
records.holdings: Te Papa's Tory Street facility includes natural-history dry stores holding microscope slides, while Te Papa Archives preserves institutional records and collected archives; Collections Online provides public object/specimen records and images.
records.research_use: A New Zealand route joining current physical slide custody to institutional archives and predecessor-museum documentation. Individual nineteenth-century slide chains can be tested against archival acquisition and correspondence records.
records.access: Collections Online is public; research visits and archive consultation are by appointment.
